## Final data-grounded hypothesis

**How did urban land use affect the invasion of different types of introduced plants?**

Urban land use in Barcelona province did not uniformly increase non-native invasion; it acted **selectively on introduced-plant type**. Increasing landscape-scale urban cover (% urban in the 1000-m buffer around plots in 2009, the operative urban-lan-use variable) raised the occurrence and count of **Unintentionally introduced** species per plot — the pathway with the strongest, most consistently positive urban association (covariate-adjusted log-count slope +0.18 per 1-SD urban, p = 0.024; presence slope +0.47 vs −0.97 for AgriForest, p < 1e−12) — had a **neutral (near-zero)** association with **Gardening/ornamental** species (−0.13 per 1-SD urban, p = 0.18) after controlling for habitat, elevation-climate, cropland, distances, and spatial position, and a **significantly negative** association with **AgriForest** (agriculture/forestry) species (−0.91, p ≈ 4.5e−18). These pathway-specific urban slopes differ robustly (Wald test that all three slopes are equal: χ² = 140.8, p = 2.7e−31), and Unintentional species are significantly more urban-responsive than Gardening species (Δslope = −0.31, p = 2.5e−5). The same ordering — Unintentional > Gardening > AgriForest — holds for local (50-m) urban cover, for the 1956 baseline (pre-urbanization) cover, and across Poisson, negative-binomial, and binomial-presence model formulations (all model runs in the executed script). Crucially, the effect is **compositional rather than addititive**: after covariate adjustment, urban cover does not predict higher *total* introduced-species richness per plot (n.total slope −0.08, p = 0.29), yet raw occurrence of introduced species is strongly urban-positive (logit +1.29, p = 7.5e−11) — so urban land use shifts the invaded-community composition toward Unintentional-type (disturbance-tolerant, anthropochorous) invaders while not favoring AgriForest types, which remain concentrated in cropland/riparian contexts (habitat means: Urban 1.60 unint / 0.69 gard / 0.03 agfo per plot). Recent active land-cover transition into urban/cropland (fraction of the 50-m buffer that changed progress between 1956–2009) shows only a weak and less robust inverse pattern for Unintentional species (count model −0.49, p = 0.014, but non-significant in presence models), indicating the association is with **established urban fabric**, not recent conversion. At the species level, Unintentional invaders are the most invasive type overall (mean 9.6 invaded plots vs 3.9 for Gardening and 2.3 for AgriForest; 6.2 ten-km cells vs 2.8 and 2.2), and phylogenetically corrected (Brownian-motion GLS on the supplied Newick tree) niche breadth is significantly higher for Unintentional than Gardening species (+0.65, p ≈ 8e−5); AgriForest species are least successful, though part of that deficit is absorbed by family/phylogenetic structure (family-fixed-effect sensitivity: −0.04, p = 0.89). Temporal-pathway context reinforces the compositional story: introductions since 1985 are overwhelmingly Gardening (397 observed vs 62.5 expected under pathway-independent rates, χ² = 230, p ≈ 6e−47), a type only intermediately coupled to urban cover — i.e., urban land use has historically favored the invasion of Unintentional-type plants already present long enough to spread (mean residence 104 yr), while the recent Gardening surge reflects propagule availability rather than urban cover per se. In short: **urban land use did not raise invasion of all introduced plants alike; it specifically facilitated invasion by unintentionally introduced species (and to a lesser extent gardening ornamentals), while suppressing or failing to promote agri-forestry species, thereby reshaping the type composition of the non-native flora.**

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded and quality-checked all four assets (temporal_trends tab-separated 12x3; invasion_success 81x19; invaded_niche tab-separated 632x37; Newick tree 81 tips). 2) Parsed the Newick into a Brownian-motion variance-covariance matrix (custom zero-dependency parser; tip labels 1:1 with species data; fixed pair-MRCA bug by keeping max shared depth). 3) Plot-level design: z-scored urban/cropland cover and Euclidean predictors; collapsed collinear elevation/temperature/rainfall into a climate PC1 (93.8% var); included habitat dummies, distances, UTM coordinates; verified VIFs (urban.2009.1000m VIF=2.9, max 4.9). 4) Fitted stacked GEE (Poisson, exchangeable within-plot, robust SE) on the 3 per-pathway counts per plot with pathway x urban interactions (primary urban.2009.1000m; sensitivity to urban.2009.50m, urban.1956.1000m, progressive 1956-2009 and 1993-2009 change flags), plus NegativeBinomial and binomial-presence GEE robustness, aggregate n.total GEE, univariate logistic/Spearman, and full-covariate per-pathway presence models. 5) Species-level negative-binomial GLMs (invaded-plots, area-of-occupancy-10km, habitat range) and OLS (invaded niche breadth) with pathway + growth form + dispersal + vegetative + height + mrt + native niche breadth; family-fixed-effect sensitivity. 6) Phylogenetic GLS on niche breadth using the tree VCV and Moran's I on OLS residuals. 7) Temporal path-contingency chi-square (4 periods x 3 pathways). 8) All numbers compiled in results_summary.json; no fabricated statistics.
